narrationScript: At its heart, the Instruction Set Architecture functions as an immutable contract between software and hardware. This contract is absolutely critical for the entire computing ecosystem. Software, whether it's a high-level compiler, an operating system, or an application, fundamentally relies on the ISA to behave in a precisely defined and consistent manner. The hardware implementation, in turn, must adhere to this contract with exact fidelity. Any deviation, even a subtle bug or 'erratum' in the hardware's interpretation or execution of the ISA, can lead to severe software failures, system instability, or security vulnerabilities. This is why the process of ISA verification is so rigorous and why processor errata are taken with such extreme seriousness by manufacturers and the industry. The ISA is not just a specification; it's the bedrock upon which all layers of abstraction in modern computing are built, ensuring that software written today can run reliably on hardware designed tomorrow, as long as both adhere to the same architectural agreement.
deliveryNotes: Stress the criticality of ISA verification
